title: XSS, CSRF, injection and tokens
subtitle: Every input is hostile until proven otherwise. See how the classic attacks work — and the one habit that stops each.

mind.title: The security mindset
mind.body: Never trust client input; give the least privilege; layer defences; fail closed. The OWASP Top 10 lists the most common flaws (broken access control, injection, cryptographic failures, insecure design, …). HTTPS protects data in transit but does nothing about these bugs.

sqli.title: SQL injection
sqli.body: Pasting input into SQL: "SELECT * FROM users WHERE name='" + n + "'" with n = ' OR '1'='1 returns every user. Fix: parameterised queries (WHERE name = ?) so the input is always data, never code.

xss.title: Cross-site scripting (XSS)
xss.body: If a site echoes user text into a page unescaped, an attacker can make it include <script> that runs in victims’ browsers with the site’s privileges (stealing cookies, acting as them). Defences: escape output for its context, a Content-Security-Policy, HttpOnly cookies, and frameworks that escape by default.

csrf.title: Cross-site request forgery (CSRF)
csrf.body: While you are logged in to a bank, a malicious page makes your browser send POST /transfer — the browser attaches your cookie automatically. Defences: a secret CSRF token in forms, SameSite cookies, re-authenticating for sensitive actions.

pw.title: Passwords and tokens
pw.body: Never store passwords in plain text: store a salted, slow hash (bcrypt, scrypt, Argon2). The salt is random per user, so identical passwords hash differently and rainbow tables fail; slowness limits guessing. Add rate limiting and multi-factor authentication. A password of length L over an alphabet of A symbols has AL possibilities.
pw.steps: Lowercase letters only (A = 26), length 8. Number of passwords ≈ 2.1 × 10¹¹; with A = 94 printable symbols it is 94⁸ ≈ 6.1 × 10¹⁵, about 29 000× more.

hdr.title: Security headers and a checklist
hdr.body:
• HTTPS everywhere with HSTS
  • Content-Security-Policy
  • Escape output, parameterise queries
  • Hash passwords with salt
  • CSRF tokens + SameSite cookies
  • Least privilege; update dependencies
